tax.isaShort: ISA tax benefits require holding at least 3 years.
notes: Regular account assumes all gains are interest/dividends. Korean listed stock gains are tax-free; foreign stock gains are taxed 22% above 2.5M KRW/yr.
ISA: up to 20M KRW/yr (unused rolls over), 100M total, 3-year minimum. Assumes one account held to the end. Proposed expansions (e.g. 5M tax-free) have not passed and are not applied.

Pension savings + IRP: up to 18M KRW/yr, credit on up to 9M. Rates assume payout from 55 over 10+ years; early termination is taxed 16.5%. Private pension over 15M KRW/yr: comprehensive tax or 16.5% separate tax.
Tax credits are added without reinvestment. Comprehensive taxation of financial income over 20M KRW/yr is not modeled.

investmentCalculator.disclaimer: This is a simple simulation assuming a constant annual return — not investment advice. Real returns vary and principal can be lost; fees and tax law changes will alter results.
investmentCalculator.title: Investment Return Calculator
investmentCalculator.description: Future value of monthly or lump-sum investing, goal solver, conservative/base/aggressive scenarios, and after-tax comparison of regular, ISA and pension accounts

concepts.title: Key Concepts
items: CAGR: Compound Annual Growth Rate, assumes steady annual growth
Lump Sum: Investing all money at once for long-term holding
DCA: Dollar Cost Averaging, investing fixed amounts monthly
Real Return: Actual purchasing power return after deducting inflation

formulas.title: Formulas
items: Lump sum: FV = PV × (1 + r)^n (annual return basis)
Monthly (paid at start of month): FV = PMT × ((1+i)^N − 1) / i × (1+i), i = monthly rate
Monthly rate i: annual basis (1+r)^(1/12) − 1, monthly compounding r/12

tips.title: Investment Tips
items: Lump sum tends to outperform DCA over longer periods
DCA reduces risk by averaging out market volatility
Consider inflation rate of 2-3% for realistic projections
Actual returns should account for taxes and fees

whatIs.title: What is the Investment Return Calculator?
whatIs.description: A tool that compounds monthly or lump-sum investments to show what they grow to in N years, and works backward to the monthly contribution, return or time needed to reach a target. It also shows conservative/base/aggressive return scenarios, inflation-adjusted value in today's money, how much you could withdraw each month, and after-tax results in a regular, ISA or pension account. Use it to gauge the long-term outcome of stocks, ETFs, funds and deposits.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select the calculation type — CAGR, compound growth simulation, target amount back-calculation, etc.
2. Enter initial investment, monthly contribution (optional), annual return rate, and investment duration.
3. To account for inflation, enter the annual inflation rate for inflation-adjusted real return.
4. Review the result graph showing principal vs. gains and year-by-year portfolio growth.

items.q: What does 500k KRW a month for 20 years become?
items.a: At a steady 7% a year, 120M KRW of principal grows to about 260M KRW. At 4% it is about 180M; at 10% about 360M.

Pension savings/IRP give a 13.2–16.5% tax credit up front but must be drawn as a pension after 55. ISA needs only a 3-year hold and gains up to 2M KRW (4M low-income) are tax-free. Check the after-tax table.
A 7% nominal return with 2% inflation is about 4.9% in purchasing power. 260M KRW in 20 years is about 170M in today's money.
A rule of thumb from past US data: withdrawing 4% of assets in year one, then adjusting for inflation, historically lasted about 30 years. Not a guarantee.
